title: What If the World Stopped Making Plastic Today?

scenes.text: What if the world stopped making plastic today? The old plastic would stay right where it is.
In 2019 the world made 460 million tonnes of plastic, double the amount in 2000.
Stopping production wouldn't touch what's already out there. About 30 million tonnes sit in seas and oceans.
Of 353 million tonnes of plastic waste in 2019, only 9 percent was recycled. About half went to landfill.
Another 22 percent went to dumps, open fires, or the environment, and 6 million tonnes leaked into rivers and seas in one year.
Stopping the flow is step one. The plastic already in the sea would still be there tomorrow.
